kit.selfHostedAuthReadsItsSettings: Self-hosted Auth reads its settings from environment variables in the stack’s .env and compose file. Projects created with “Create a new stack” are configured here.
kit.supermixerConnectsToThisStackSo: Supermixer connects to this stack, so its Auth settings are set where it runs
kit.onlyOwnersAndAdministratorsCanChange: Only Owners and Administrators can change Auth settings
kit.savedSettingsTakeEffectWhenIt: Saved settings take effect when it starts.
kit.savedItTakesEffectWhenThe: Saved; it takes effect when the stack starts

users.emailsALinkToSetA: Emails a link to set a new password. Needs SMTP on the stack.
users.emailsAOneTimeSignIn: Emails a one-time sign-in link. Needs SMTP on the stack.
users.marksTheEmailAsVerifiedWithout: Marks the email as verified without sending anything, e.g. when the stack has no SMTP.
users.letsTheUserSignInAgain: Lets the user sign in again.
users.stopsTheUserSigningInOr: Stops the user signing in or refreshing sessions for a while.
users.removesTheUserAndTheirSessions: Removes the user and their sessions. Rows referencing them may block it.
users.theyCanTSignInOr: They can't sign in or refresh their session {{phrase}}.
users.thisCanTBeUndoneThe: This can't be undone. The user's sessions end at once.
users.sendsAnEmailWithALink: Sends an email with a link to set up their account. The stack needs SMTP configured.
users.theUserCanSignInWith: The user can sign in with this email and password straight away.
users.sentToTheStackSAuth: Sent to the stack's Auth service over the gateway; Auth hashes it.
users.autoConfirmUserMarksTheEmail: Auto confirm userMarks the email as verified now. Auth sends no email for users created here, so if you untick this, confirm them later from their details or they can't sign in.

authAuditLogs.whatHappenedInAuthSignUps: What happened in Auth: sign-ups, sign-ins, changes to users and more, from Auth's own audit table.
authAuditLogs.searchEmailUserIdOrIp: Search email, user ID or IP
authAuditLogs.noAuditEntriesYetIfAuth: No audit entries yet. If Auth runs with GOTRUE_AUDIT_LOG_DISABLE_POSTGRES, it doesn’t write them here.

authHooks.runsBeforeATokenIsIssued: Runs before a token is issued; add or change its claims.
authHooks.runsBeforeAUserIsCreated: Runs before a user is created; can reject the sign-up.
authHooks.runsOnEachMfaAttemptCan: Runs on each MFA attempt; can reject it, for example after too many failures.
authHooks.runsOnEachPasswordSignIn: Runs on each password sign-in; can reject it.
authHooks.sendsSmsMessagesYourselfInsteadOf: Sends SMS messages yourself instead of through the SMS provider.
authHooks.sendsEmailsYourselfInsteadOfThrough: Sends emails yourself instead of through SMTP.
authHooks.runYourOwnPostgresFunctionOr: Run your own Postgres function or HTTP endpoint at points in the Auth flow.
authHooks.aPostgresFunctionPgFunctionsPostgres: A Postgres function, pg-functions://postgres/public/my_hook (grant it to supabase_auth_admin), or an HTTPS endpoint.
authHooks.forHttpEndpointsV1WhsecUsed: For HTTP endpoints: v1,whsec_<base64>, used to sign requests (Standard Webhooks).

authMfa.secondFactorsUsersCanAddTo: Second factors users can add to their accounts.
authMfa.usersCanAddAnAuthenticatorApp: Users can add an authenticator app
authMfa.usersCanSignInWithAn: Users can sign in with an authenticator app
authMfa.needsAnSmsProviderSignIn: Needs an SMS provider (Sign In / Providers › Phone).
authMfa.usersCanAddAPhoneNumber: Users can add a phone number
authMfa.usersCanSignInWithA: Users can sign in with a code sent by SMS

authProtection.lowercaseUppercaseLettersDigitsAndSymbol: Lowercase, uppercase letters, digits and symbols
authProtection.requiresACaptchaTokenFromYour: Requires a CAPTCHA token from your app on sign-up, sign-in and password reset.
authProtection.rejectsPasswordsFoundInHaveibeenpwnedOrg: Rejects passwords found in HaveIBeenPwned.org’s breach data. Auth sends the first 5 characters of the password’s SHA-1 hash, never the password.

authProviders.howUsersSignUpAndSign: How users sign up and sign in.
authProviders.allowNewUsersToSignUp: Allow new users to sign up
authProviders.whenOffOnlyInvitedOrAdmin: When off, only invited or admin-created users can sign in.
authProviders.usersCanStartASessionWithout: Users can start a session without an email or phone, and link one later.
authProviders.usersMustConfirmTheirEmailAddress: Users must confirm their email address before they can sign in. Needs a working SMTP server (Emails).
authProviders.signInWithEmailAndPassword: Sign in with email and password, magic links or one-time codes.
authProviders.changingEmailNeedsConfirmationFromBoth: Changing email needs confirmation from both the old and the new address.
authProviders.changingPasswordNeedsARecentSign: Changing password needs a recent sign-in or a one-time code.
authProviders.signInWithAOneTime: Sign in with a one-time code sent by SMS.
authProviders.usersMustConfirmTheirPhoneNumber: Users must confirm their phone number before they can sign in.
authProviders.registerTheCallbackUrlBelowWith: Register the callback URL below with each provider, then paste its client ID and secret here.
authProviders.setBySupermixerFromTheStack: Set by Supermixer from the stack's API URL.

authRateLimits.limitsOnAuthSEndpointsTo: Limits on Auth's endpoints, to stop abuse. Empty means Auth's default.
authRateLimits.signUpConfirmationsMagicLinksPassword: Sign-up confirmations, magic links, password resets and invites, for the whole project. Only applies with your own SMTP server.

authSessions.howLongUsersStaySignedIn: How long users stay signed in, and how refresh tokens behave.
authSessions.detectAndRevokeCompromisedRefreshTokens: Detect and revoke compromised refresh tokens
authSessions.eachRefreshTokenCanBeUsed: Each refresh token can be used once; reusing an old one signs out the whole session.
authSessions.howLongAnOldRefreshToken: How long an old refresh token still works, for clients that retry or race.
authSessions.signUsersOutAfterThisLong: Sign users out after this long, however active they are.
authSessions.signUsersOutAfterThisLong2: Sign users out after this long without refreshing their session.
authSessions.signingInEndsTheUserS: Signing in ends the user’s other sessions; only the newest stays signed in.

authTemplates.theSmtpServerAuthSendsThrough: The SMTP server Auth sends through, and the emails it sends.
authTemplates.supabaseSExampleSettingsPointAt: Supabase's example settings point at a mail server that doesn't exist, so Auth can't send email until this is set.
authTemplates.minimumIntervalBetweenEmailsToThe: Minimum interval between emails to the same user
authTemplates.emptyFieldsUseAuthSBuilt: Empty fields use Auth's built-in emails. Templates use Go template syntax.
authTemplates.subject: Subject
authTemplates.templateTagsAppearAsWrittenScripts: Template tags appear as written; scripts don't run.

authUrlConfiguration.whereAuthSendsUsersAfterThey: Where Auth sends users after they sign in, confirm their email or reset their password.
authUrlConfiguration.theDefaultRedirectUrlUsedWhen: The default redirect URL, used when a request names none or one that isn't allowed. Also {{siteUrl}} in email templates.
authUrlConfiguration.otherUrlsAuthMayRedirectTo: Other URLs Auth may redirect to, such as preview deploys or a mobile app's deep link. Wildcards work: * matches within a path segment, ** across segments.
authUrlConfiguration.startWithAScheme: Start with a scheme, like https:// or myapp://

authUsers.everyoneWhoHasSignedUpTo: Everyone who has signed up to this project, from Auth's own tables.
authUsers.searchEmailPhoneNameOrId: Search email, phone, name or ID
authUsers.noUsersYetUsersAppearHere: No users yet. Users appear here when they sign up, or when you add them.
